item_id: Unique key for an item. Everything joins on it.
lot_id: Key for a purchased batch. Items in one lot share price, source and condition mix, so cross-validation never splits a lot.
category: Biggest driver of recovery and of how fast something sells. Also the level at which markdown rules and minimum-value rules are set.
brand_tier: Premium brands hold value and match to the catalog more reliably than generic ones.
condition: Tested condition after the warehouse grades it. Strongly shifts both the chance of a sale and the price.
retail_value: The denominator of the recovery rate and the best single size signal. Also decides whether extra handling or photos can pay for themselves.
log_retail_value: Log of retail value: lets the model treat a $20 and a $2,000 item proportionally.
match_confidence: How sure the catalog match is. A wrong match corrupts the target, so low confidence widens uncertainty.
product_age_years: Older models depreciate: recovery falls with age, differently by category.
title: Free text the staff type. Reduced to 8 numeric components so wording (model line, bundle, 'for parts') can inform the price.
matched_title: The catalog entry the item was matched to. Used only by the match-quality model to compare against the listing title.
return_reason: Why it came back. Defective returns recover less. Marked 'ask': confirm with the business that it is captured at receipt.
weight_class: 0 tiny to 4 bulky. Drives shipping and storage cost and sets how heavy holding is.
photo_count: Listing photos. Tested with a randomized experiment, not just observed, because staff photograph valuable items more.
receipt_to_listing_days: Days sitting in the warehouse before listing. Slow listing hurts timing and ties up cash.
start_bid_pct: Opening bid as a share of retail value. Sets the floor and affects the chance of zero bids.
auction_duration_days: Auction length. Changes how many bidders see the item.
end_dow: Day of week the auction ends. Weekend endings pull more bidders.
simultaneous_listings: Items of the same category listed in the same week. A supply glut lowers prices.
listing_moy: Month of year: seasonality. Also a drift alarm, because it changes every year.
source_id: Which supplier. Sources differ in quality; used by the scorecard and, with care, by the models.
source_type: Big-box returns, e-commerce returns, overstock, broker liquidation, regional marketplace. The group-level view of quality.
region: Where the source sits. Affects freight and, after expansion, demand.
manifest_flag: Whether the lot came with an item list. Blind lots are riskier and priced differently.
acquisition_rate: Lot price divided by lot retail value: what we paid per retail dollar. Known at receipt, so it may feed prediction.
lot_item_count: Items in the lot, for lot-level modelling.
pilot_arm: Which arm of the randomized fixed-price pilot the item was in (fixed-price or auction control). Context for the uplift analysis only.
premium_pct: Premium over expected auction price for fixed-price items (10/20/30%), randomized. Identifies price response.
photo_arm: Which arm of the photo experiment (extra photos or control). Randomized, so the effect is causal.
handling_minutes: Warehouse labor minutes per item. Valued at the labor cost per minute. A cost, never an input to a prediction.
fees: Marketplace fees. A cost and a sale-time quantity: not usable for prediction.
shipping_cost: Outbound shipping. A cost known only after the sale.
holding_days: Days the item occupied shelf space until it closed. Drives holding and capital cost. Known only after the sale.
bidders: Number of bidders. An outcome of the auction: never a predictor.
watchers: People watching during the listing. Known too late to price the item.
sale_price: What the item sold for. The numerator of recovery. The target, so it can never be an input.
sold: Whether it sold. Zero outcomes are final for auctions.
refund_flag: Whether a sold item was refunded. Known after the sale.
